A long a. It also carries hamza (أ إ) at the start of words that begin with a vowel.
Two dots above. Dental, like Spanish t.
Three dots above. [θ] as in "think" in Standard Arabic; Levantine usually says [t] or [s].
One dot above, with a deeper bowl at the end of a word.
Two dots below. A consonant [j], or the long vowels [iː] and [eː].
One dot inside. Levantine [ʒ] as in "measure"; Standard [dʒ].
No dot. The squeezed throat h.
Doesn't join to the next letter.
Like د with a dot. [ð] as in "this" in Standard Arabic; Levantine [d] or [z].
Doesn't join to the next letter. Tapped or trilled.
Like ر with a dot. Doesn't join to the next letter.
Doesn't join to the next letter. A consonant [w], or the long vowels [uː] and [oː].
The emphatic s: a loop then a tooth.
The emphatic t: a loop with an upright stroke.
Like ط with a dot. Levantine [zˤ]; Standard [ðˤ].
An open hook. Its shape changes a lot between positions.
Two dots above, deeper tail than ف. Levantine [ʔ] in most words; Standard [q].
Has a small hamza-like mark inside when isolated or final.
A tall stroke with a hook. ل + ا is written as one ligature: لا.
Changes shape a lot: ه هـ ـهـ ـه.
The glottal stop. Sits on its own or on a "seat": أ إ ؤ ئ.
